title: Citrine - latency drift and priority fallback workshop
summary: Follow-up workshop to review recent 11/02 latency drift affecting low-priority model routes. We validated root cause as spiky KV cache misses and an autoscaler mis-smoothing, agreed on short-term mitigations (priority fallback routing, temporary batch cap) and medium-term fixes (cache checksum monitor, autoscaler smoothing tweak, quantized model variant rollout). Action items assigned and a pilot for the fallback rule to run for ~2 weeks.
topics: KV cache miss patterns and monitoring
action_items: Maya Patel - Share filtered trace deck and canary config snippets - 2025-11-06
Tom Reyes - Run KV cache checksum sweep across canary cluster and upload logs - 2025-11-07
Luca Moretti - Implement temporary priority-fallback route and verify routing metrics - 2025-11-10
Mei Lin - Confirm encryption/KMS handoff for fallback logging and sign off on audit config - 2025-11-12
Ravi Gupta - Provide success criteria for pilot (p95 < 300ms for critical routes) - 2025-11-06
next_steps: Redwood to deploy priority-fallback rule to Citrine canary cluster by 2025-11-06
Customer to run KV cache checksum and share findings in shared doc (link in chat)
Schedule 2-week pilot review on 2025-11-20 to evaluate telemetry
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Luca Moretti, Jordan Lee (Redwood) — Aisha Khan, Tom Reyes, Ravi Gupta, Mei Lin (Citrine)

Auto Summary: brief incident re-run, action list creation, fallback pilot agreement.

[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick check, audio ok?
[00:05] Aisha Khan: yes, can hear you, thanks. we wanted this to be square one after that drift on sunday, we had significant tail latency on our low-pri routes.
[00:18] Luca Moretti: quick context — we pulled traces and saw a pattern of K V cache misses then a burst of CPU during token gen, so tails spiked. also the autoscaler smoothing didn't step in quickly because of the smoothing window.
[00:35] Tom Reyes: yeah that matches what we saw, we had a couple of pods that were effectively cold and then the batching hit higher queuing and everything slowed.
[00:48] Ravi Gupta: just to clarify, which routes are "low-pri"? those are the summarization-only endpoints, right? not PHI-handling ones?
[00:58] Aisha Khan: correct, health-data routes are isolated; this was user-summaries and suggestions only.
[01:10] Mei Lin: security note — if we fallback to another model we need to make sure logs don't contain PII. is that covered by the fallback config?
[01:20] Maya Patel: good call. our fallback rule can redact request payloads and only emit aggregated telemetry; we'll share the exact audit config, Luca will own that example.
[01:35] Luca Moretti: yeah i have a snippet, it's in the shared sandbox repo — link in chat. the rule uses priority tags, if capacity below threshold it routes to a quantized variant with lower token throughput but much cheaper and stable latency.
[01:55] Tom Reyes: the quantized variant — any impact on answer quality? we've got product teams worried about hallucinations increasing.
[02:05] Luca Moretti: expected small regressions on edge cases; we'll pair rollout with a small eval set that Ravi will provide. quality monitors will run we can auto rollback if metric drift > threshold.
[02:25] Aisha Khan: can we get a quick run through of the KV cache checksum idea? Tom ran a script on sunday but it was noisy.
[02:34] Tom Reyes: it flagged about 0.8% of entries as mismatched across pods. again noise, but could be contributing to misses.
[02:42] Maya Patel: that sounds high, Luca, is that within normal jitter or symptomatic?
[02:47] Luca Moretti: it's above baseline; the cache sharding maintainer had a race when a pod restarted that might leave stale shards until reconcilation. also some eviction thrash when sequence length jumped.
[03:05] Ravi Gupta: eviction thrash meaning large requests pushing old prefixes out?
[03:09] Luca Moretti: yeah exactly. we saw longer prefixes cause more KV churn. quantization reduces seq len slightly since tokenization differs, might help as side-effect.
[03:25] Maya Patel: proposed short-term mitigations: 1) temporary cap on batch size for low-pri routes, 2) priority-fallback routing to quantized variant, 3) run cache checksum sweep nightly for a week. any objections?
[03:42] Aisha Khan: sounds reasonable as a stop-gap, we want minimal product impact.
[03:47] Mei Lin: need to sign off on the logging change first, can't stream full requests during fallback.
[03:52] Jordan Lee: we'll include redaction and aggregated counters only. i will draft audit fields.
[04:05] Tom Reyes: timeline? we can get the checksum script running today and share raw logs, but we'd prefer redwood to deploy the fallback to canary first.
[04:14] Luca Moretti: we can push the priority-fallback rule to the Citrine canary cluster by thursday, 11/06. we'll include toggles.
[04:23] Ravi Gupta: good. for the quality eval, i'll send a 200-example set and pass/fail criteria. p95 goal for critical routes is 300ms — is that realistic with fallback?
[04:35] Luca Moretti: yes, fallback to quantized should keep p95 under that for heavy bursts, unless backend I/O flaps.
[04:44] Aisha Khan: competitor question — some teams looked at ApexAI and CloudEndeavor; think they offer similar fallback at infra level, any material difference?
[04:53] Maya Patel: short answer: we tend to integrate fallback at routing layer paired with KV awareness and per-token economics. other vendors do node-level preemption; different tradeoffs.
[05:05] Tom Reyes: okay. can we also tune autoscaler smoothing? the current window is too long.
[05:12] Luca Moretti: yes we recommend reducing smoothing from 90s to 30s for the low-pri pool and adding a small warmup pod to reduce cold starts. we'll provide exact helm values.
[05:25] Ravi Gupta: any risk to cost from reducing smoothing?
[05:28] Maya Patel: slight increase during steady state but overall expected to lower tail cost by preventing long queues — net positive.
[05:38] Mei Lin: are we confident fallback won't leak data between models? we've seen model variants share cache keys before.
[05:45] Luca Moretti: we will namespace KV keys per model variant and clear cross-variant cache on deploy. also we'll ensure KMS usage for any persisted traces.
[05:58] Aisha Khan: ok action item recap please
[06:02] Maya Patel: sure — Maya to share traces and config snippets, Tom to run checksum and share logs, Luca to deploy fallback to canary, Mei to confirm KMS/audit config, Ravi to send eval set. pilot review 11/20.
[06:20] Tom Reyes: quick note, we saw a correlated increase in external HTTP calls from our enrichment service during the spike, might be related. we'll include that in the KV logs.
[06:30] Maya Patel: good catch. please attach any enrichment traces — could be amplification.
[06:36] Jordan Lee: i'll put all artifacts in the shared folder: /shared/citrine/incident-20251102 including a short runbook for the fallback toggle. link: https://redwood.example.com/sandbox/citrine-incident (internal)
[06:50] Ravi Gupta: thanks everyone. any blockers on schedule?
[06:54] Aisha Khan: none from our side, we want to keep pilot limited while we validate metrics.
[07:02] Luca Moretti: we'll also add an alert if fallback applied for >10% of traffic for >15m.
[07:10] Mei Lin: add me to any security PRs.
[07:15] Maya Patel: noted. final quick ask: Tom, can you prioritize the checksum results so Luca can tune the cache reconciliation?
[07:23] Tom Reyes: yes, will do by friday.
[07:27] Maya Patel: great, thanks all. we'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invite for the 11/20 review.

End of transcript.

References: shared folder link above, canary config snippet (attached in chat), short trace deck (will be emailed).

Transcript notes: some words may be mis-transcribed (e.g., K V cache as "K V" or "kv"), acronyms occasionally spaced (S A M L), minor speaker mis-attribution possible.
